# Rakshith Bangalore

> Rakshith Bangalore is a robotics engineer and entrepreneur in the United Kingdom and Singapore. The work covers humanoid robots (Unitree H1-2 and G1 on a PepsiCo programme), robot simulation (WardZero), Industry 4.0 mobile manipulation, medical robotics, and the delivery of AI software and hardware products (software project management with JIRA, Confluence and Miro; hardware product management with BOM, DFM and US market entry). Rakshith hosts Unfiltered Robotics, a podcast on legged robots and hardware development.

Facts:
- Latest project: WardZero, an open platform to develop and test hospital robots in simulation. It has a simulated hospital with a surgical wing, Isaac Sim and MuJoCo, a safety layer and ROS 2 navigation. The reference robot is a Unitree G1 humanoid with BrainCo Revo2 hands. All tests used simulation only.
- Professional humanoid R&D: neural policies for legged control, sim-to-real transfer and actuator identification on Unitree H1-2 and G1.
- Industry 4.0 mobile manipulator (award-winning MEng capstone): UR-10 arm on an Omron LD250 base with SmartShift tool changing, scoped with Walkers around a live factory workflow.
- Laparoscopic surgery trainer: compliant force-feedback mechanism, an eight-month project with an NHS Trust.
- Aircraft cabin lab: a decommissioned Embraer ERJ 145 converted into a flight-comfort research platform (EU Clean Sky 2, Comfdemo).
- Product delivery: an AI-enabled full-stack post-production software platform (pilot post-production reduced from 4 days to 4 hours) and a portable podcasting solution moving to its first production run.
- Education: MEng, Nottingham Trent University.
